ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a 3×3 grid magic square. The upper-left cell is labeled a, the cell on the right side of the middle row is 47, the middle cell of the bottom row is 63, and the remaining cells are empty. Reasoning: The problem states that the sums of each row, each column, and each diagonal are all the same. According to the standard parameterization of a 3×3 magic square, if the center is m and the two offsets are p, q, then the related positions can be written as: upper-left corner a=m+p, middle right side is m+p−q, bottom middle is m+p+q. Therefore the upper-left corner a equals the average of these two visible numbers: a=(47+63)/2=110/2=55.

Therefore the upper-left cell equals the average of those two visible adjacent edge cells: a=(47+63)/2=55.
